what_its_for: Meclizine is used to prevent and treat nausea, vomiting, and dizziness caused by motion sickness. It is also used to treat dizziness and spinning sensations (vertigo) caused by inner ear problems.
how_to_take: Take meclizine by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole or chew it if using a chewable tablet. If you are taking it for motion sickness, take it at least 1 hour before you travel. Drink a full glass of water with each dose.
dosing: For motion sickness in adults and children 12 years and older: Take 25 to 50 mg about 1 hour before traveling. You may repeat the dose every 24 hours as needed during your trip. For vertigo in adults: Take 25 to 100 mg per day, divided into doses as directed by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store meclizine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medicine that is past its expiration date.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking meclizine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleeping pills, anxiety medicines, or muscle relaxers, unless your doctor approves. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience severe drowsiness that affects your daily life, difficulty urinating or no urination, blurred vision or eye pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, confusion or hallucinations, a severe allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your dizziness or nausea does not improve or gets worse.
when_it_works: Meclizine usually begins to work within 1 hour of taking it. For motion sickness, it works best when taken at least 1 hour before traveling. Its effects can last up to 24 hours.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with caution, as meclizine can cause more drowsiness, confusion, dizziness, and increased risk of falls in people over 65. A lower dose may be recommended. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using meclizine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as its safety in these situations is not fully established. Children: Meclizine is generally not recommended for children under 12 years of age unless directed by a doctor. Kidney or liver problems: Let your doctor know if you have any kidney or liver issues before using this medicine.
